note: Editorial registry of every vintage under data/. It is not part of any hash. It is append-only: a new vintage adds an entry; an existing entry may only gain superseded_by links and warnings; nothing is removed or rewritten. Published vintage files are never edited. See SPEC.md, 'Corrections and supersession'.

warnings.detail: Counts 20 euro-area member states. Bulgaria joined the euro area on 2026-01-01, so on both FX dates (2026-01-09, 2026-05-15) it had 21 members; Bulgaria's 6667660 persons (UN WPP 2024) are missing.
UN WPP 2024 figures were taken from Worldometer's republication, not from the UN Population Division's file.
2 of 25 populations differ from the UN file by 1 person: Greece 9897115 vs 9897116, Slovenia 2114573 vs 2114574.
Counts 20 euro-area member states in both the headcount and the population-weighted PPP blend; Bulgaria (a member since 2026-01-01) is missing.
UN WPP 2024 figures were taken from Worldometer's republication (the same numbers as v0.1, including the two 1-person differences from the UN file).

Labels its World Bank PA.NUS.PPP 2024 values 'ICP 2024' (SOURCES.md; ppp_status in the hashed spec). No ICP 2024 results have been released (latest ICP cycle: 2021, released May 2024). In WDI the 2024 values are the ICP 2021 benchmark extrapolated to 2024 by the World Bank for China and India, and Eurostat-OECD annual PPPs for Japan, the United Kingdom and the euro-area members; the United States is 1 by definition. See docs/AUDIT.md (2026-10-26).

Its 25 PA.NUS.PPP 2024 values equal the WDI release of April 2026. The World Bank revised 5 of them in the July 2026 release (unchanged as of the 2026-10-08 update): China 3.5325492491585 -> 3.52537888953537, India 20.4219876045922 -> 20.4522424138694, and Croatia, Cyprus and Malta by 0.0003% or less.

Its CNY and INR PPP factors are the ICP 2021 benchmark extrapolated to 2024 by the World Bank, not benchmark values; the World Bank will replace them when the next ICP cycle's results are released and revised them between its April and July 2026 releases. The other factors are Eurostat-OECD annual PPPs, which can also be revised.
